page.layout: One printed page (right-hand page, p. 481 of the book). Running head at the top. Below it a centred two-line title, "HISTORIA IMPLEMENTI.", then one column of running text with a decorated initial at the start. No marginal notes. Catchword at the lower right, signature at the foot.

main_text.l: HISTORIA
IMPLEMENTI.
§. 1. L[?]icet nondum omnium rerum cernamus
finem, ac nesciamus quid serus advectu-
rus sit vesper, nisi in quantum nobis a-
liqua futurorum spes facta est per scri-
pturas propheticas: nihilominus hic loci quaedam no-
tanda sunt, ut hactenus per historiam Novi Testamen-
ti confirmata.
1. Videas hic ut errorem notari sententiam de usu simulacrorum
Doctrinali, atque quosdam hic repraesentari sub N.
Test. ab errore revocandos. Praevidit itaque
in spiritu Propheta simulacra in ecclesiam introducenda,
& sub hoc colore à quibusdam retinenda. Nec vana
fuit illa praevisio: quam primum enim à simplicitate
primitivae trium anteriorum seculorum ecclesiae (quae
nulla admisit in ecclesiis simulacra, ut à variis demon-
stratum est) inceperunt recedere Christiani, & in sacris
divitias ostentare pace Constantini acquisitas, augusta
sacris condita sunt templa, & pretiosa quaesita or-
namenta, peristromata nempe, & vela, quandoqui-
dem acupicta, quae spontaneorum munificentia liberali
manu attulit. Cumque inter ea in Hispania maturè e-
tiam picturae numerarentur, cavit Concilium Eliberitanum
picturas reciperent aut admitterent: ita enim praecipit
canon istius Conc. 36. Placuit picturas in ecclesiis esse

page.notes: The decorated initial is a large ornamental letter; the first letter is likely L (Licet), marked [?]. The "1." before "Videas" is a printed paragraph number and is kept in the text. Long s is written as plain s throughout. The line "pisse," is the catchword, so it is not repeated in the text. The printed hyphen in "ru-" is kept as printed, and the word continues on the next page. "acupicta" and "reciperent" are printed in this form and are left as they are.
